_about: Plain-language questions mapped to 38 CFR Part 4 rating criteria. Ask the Veteran to pick what is TRUE on a typical day and on bad days (flare-ups). Never suggest an answer, never explain which answer pays more, and never pressure. 'maps_to' is for Claude only; do not show it. Verify criteria against the bundled CFR before use. Created by EhrenAL. JOSHUAONENINE

common.q: How often do you have bad days (flare-ups) with this condition?
options: Several times a week or daily
common.maps_to: Flare-ups are considered for functional loss (38 CFR 4.40, 4.45, 4.59)

questions.q: Does your knee give way, buckle or feel unstable?
Did a doctor or physical therapist PRESCRIBE a brace, cane, crutches or walker for your knee?
options: I use one, but it wasn't prescribed
questions.maps_to: 5257: brace/assistive device prescribed changes the level

questions.q: Does your knee lock or catch, or swell up with fluid?
questions.maps_to: 5258 (dislocated cartilage: locking, pain, effusion) / 5259 symptomatic removal

questions.q: On bad days, how far can you bend your knee?
questions.maps_to: 5260/5261 motion; the exam measures it, so this is supporting lay evidence

spine.cfr: part-4/4.71a.md (General Rating Formula for the Spine)

questions.q: On bad days, how far can you bend forward?
questions.maps_to: Forward flexion ranges in the General Rating Formula

Do you have pain, numbness or tingling that travels into an arm or leg?
questions.maps_to: Note (1): rate associated neurologic problems (radiculopathy) separately

questions.q: Any bowel or bladder problems you think come from your back?
Which is your dominant (writing) hand?
questions.maps_to: Major vs minor arm ratings differ

Does your shoulder slip or pop out of place?
On bad days, how far can you lift your knee toward your chest?
Can you cross your legs or turn your foot out?

Which is your dominant (writing) hand?

mental.cfr: part-4/4.130.md (General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders)

questions.q: Which of these do you deal with? Check all that apply. You can skip this.
questions.maps_to: Symptom examples in the General Rating Formula. If 'thoughts of death or self-harm' is checked, show the TAKE A BREAK block with the Veterans Crisis Line FIRST.

questions.q: How much does it affect work?
How much does it affect family and friends?
Which of these do you have since the head injury? Check all that apply.
questions.maps_to: 8045 cognitive facets and subjective symptoms; avoid double-counting with PTSD (4.14)

questions.q: During a bad headache, do you have to stop what you're doing and lie down?
How often does that happen, on average over the last few months?
Have headaches caused you to miss work or leave early?
Is the ringing there most of the time or does it come back often?

options: Yes, but I don't use it

Has a doctor found a narrowing (stricture) of your esophagus, or stretched it (dilation)?

questions.q: Do you take medicine every day for reflux?
Do you have trouble swallowing?
How many of your scars are painful?
Does the skin over any scar break open or wear away often?
Do any scars limit movement or cause other problems?

impact._about: Asked for EVERY claim. Functional impact on work and relationships supports every rating (38 CFR 4.10), is the core of mental-health ratings (4.130), and matters for extra-schedular (3.321(b)) and TDIU (4.16) decisions. Ask what is true; never suggest answers.

work.q: How does your <condition> affect your job (military or civilian)? Check all that apply.
options: Can't do some parts of my job
Miss work, leave early, or need appointments
On a profile / limited duty / job changed
Need accommodations (breaks, standing desk, no lifting)
Changed jobs or was let go

relationships.q: How does your <condition> affect your close relationships? Check all that apply. You can skip this.
options: Can't play sports or do active things with my kids or family
Can't do other activities with my spouse/partner or kids
Pull away from family or friends
Skip social events, trips, or church

active_family._about: For physical conditions, ask about active family life FIRST and by name, with an example in the description. It shows real loss of function (38 CFR 4.10, 4.40) and is often the most convincing part of a statement.
active_family.option: Can't play sports or do active things with my kids or family
active_family.examples: coaching or playing ball with the kids, jogging together, hiking, biking, swimming, carrying or lifting kids, rough-housing, yard games
active_family.follow_up: Which activities did you used to do with them that you can't do now, or do less? (type them, or Skip)

daily.q: How does it affect daily life? Check all that apply.

example.q: Want to add one real example, in your own words? (For example: 'I can't help coach my kids and jog with them in practice anymore.') This is often the most convincing part of a statement.
